text:
support_jen: FYI customer #C-12345 reporting sudden p95/p99 latency regressions on hosted/v1/generate for model `redwood-xl-4k` since ~09:10 UTC. p95 ~140ms -> 680ms, p99 up to 1.2s. No error codes in their app, just timeouts / slow responses. Attached graph and example request IDs.

*taylor:* Can you paste one of the slow request IDs? Also which region and deployment?

support_jen: request_id=rid_9a2c7f, region=us-west-2, deployment=d-prod-01. Customer repro steps: repeated single-turn prompt with prefix "Invoice: <customer>" shows variability. They saw it on ~150 requests over 30m.

sre-oncall: seeing cluster-wide p95 bump correlated with KV cache miss-rate spike on nodes in d-prod-01. Cache metrics: prefix_cache_miss_rate 0.61 -> 0.89 across pods 12:09-12:25 UTC. Hotset churn + high eviction rate.

aditya: any config changes around 12:00? autoscale? quant?

ops-bot: Deploy event: scale-up triggered at 11:58 UTC for d-prod-01 (autoscaler), config unchanged.

maria: I pulled logs. There's a pattern: incoming prompts include user-provided metadata header X-Request-Context with slightly different casing/ordering. Cache key builder uses raw headers + prompt prefix -> many distinct keys for same logical prefix. Example in logs:
```
cache_key = f"{model}:{prefix}:{headers}"\n# header samples: "x-request-context:acct=42" vs "X-Request-Context: acct=42"
```
Result: same logical prefix split across many keys, hot-key spread and eviction thrash.

taylor: Ugh. That matches a previous bug where we didn't normalize header casing/trailing spaces in prefix hash. Does telemetry show identical text prefix hash grouping?

sre-oncall: prefix_hash_cardinality jumped x12. KV evictions/sec increased 8x. p50 unchanged, but p95/p99 correlate tightly with miss spikes.

aditya: Mitigations: immediate and short-term: 1) enable conservative caching by switching eviction policy to LFU on d-prod-01 to favor repeated logical prefixes 2) extend TTL for prefix entries from 2m -> 10m 3) run a normalization hotfix in runtime to canonicalize header keys (fast patch). Which can we do immediately?

maria: We can flip TTL + eviction policy via runtime flags in ~5m with no restart. Normalization patch needs a quick PR and canary deploy (non-trivial but doable in ~45m).

taylor: Suggest order: flip flags now to reduce thrash, run a warmup script to repopulate hot prefixes, then deploy normalization to eliminate root cause. We'll need to coordinate with support to avoid double-counting traffic.

aditya: I'll run the flags change and warmup. Warmup script is basically replay of representative prefixes & short prompts to bring KV hotset back. Script (run from bastion):
```
for p in prefixes.txt; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_KEY" -H "X-Request-Context: acct=42" -d "{\"prompt\": \"$p example\"}" https://d-prod-01.api.redwood/v1/generate &
done
```

sre-oncall: I'll add a temporary alert: prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.5 && p95_latency > 400ms -> pager, and raise threshold back after stabilization. Also enabling more verbose cache debug logs for 15m to capture any remaining anomalies.

support_jen: Told customer we have a mitigation plan: flipping runtime flags + warmup then patch. They requested ETA for full fix.

maria: Quick repro: I reproduced locally by sending same logical prefix with varying header casing; miss rate jumps and I can reproduce p95 jump in a dev pod. I'll open PR for header normalization: small function to lowercase header names and trim spaces before building cache key. PR link: (will post).

taylor: Good. Action items: aditya (flip flags + run warmup) -> in progress, maria (PR + canary) -> working, sre-oncall (monitor + alert) -> done, support_jen (customer comms) -> updated. Post-mortem if customer still sees >5% error/latency SLA violation after normalization.

ops-bot: Flag update: eviction_policy=dprod01 -> LFU applied at 12:34 UTC; prefix_ttl increased to 600s.

aditya: warmup started 12:36 UTC (script sending 5k representative requests). Monitoring shows prefix_cache_miss_rate dropping to 0.22 after warmup, p95 down to ~170ms within 6 minutes.

sre-oncall: kept verbose cache logs for 15m, captured header-case variants and normalized keys in traces. No further thrash. Will keep alert enabled for 1h.

maria: PR opened: fix/normalize-cache-keys (#987). Rolling canary scheduled to 2% traffic in 40m.

support_jen: Customer updated: saw improvement, will validate more load tonight. They asked for permanent mitigation timeline: normalization patch + canary -> full roll in ~2h if green.

taylor: Great work. Post-action note: long-term we should avoid including raw headers in cache key unless canonicalized or use a stable fingerprint. Add a backlog ticket for cache-key sanitization + tests + add unit tests for header variants.

sre-oncall: Closing loop: p95 returned to baseline ~150ms, p99 ~350ms, miss_rate stable. Will follow up in postmortem doc.

aditya: marking thread resolved for now.

ops-bot: Incident ticket C-12345 escalated -> resolved (mitigated) at 12:45 UTC.
